NKJV.1: Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, And let the hills hear your voice.
NKJV.2: Hear, O you mountains, the LORD’s complaint, And you strong foundations of the earth; For the LORD has a complaint against His people, And He will contend with Israel.
NKJV.3: “O My people, what have I done to you? And how have I wearied you? Testify against Me.
NKJV.4: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt, I redeemed you from the house of bondage; And I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
NKJV.5: O My people, remember now What Balak king of Moab counseled, And what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, From Acacia Grove to Gilgal, That you may know the righteousness of the LORD.”
NKJV.6: With what shall I come before the LORD, And bow myself before the High God? Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings, With calves a year old?
NKJV.7: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, Ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
NKJV.8: He has shown you, O man, what is good; And what does the LORD require of you But to do justly, To love mercy, And to walk humbly with your God?
NKJV.9: The LORD’s voice cries to the city— Wisdom shall see Your name: “Hear the rod! Who has appointed it?
NKJV.10: Are there yet the treasures of wickedness In the house of the wicked, And the short measure that is an abomination?
NKJV.11: Shall I count pure those with the wicked scales, And with the bag of deceitful weights?
NKJV.12: For her rich men are full of violence, Her inhabitants have spoken lies, And their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
NKJV.13: “Therefore I will also make you sick by striking you, By making you desolate because of your sins.
NKJV.14: You shall eat, but not be satisfied; Hunger shall be in your midst. You may carry some away, but shall not save them; And what you do rescue I will give over to the sword.
NKJV.15: “You shall sow, but not reap; You shall tread the olives, but not anoint yourselves with oil; And make sweet wine, but not drink wine.
NKJV.16: For the statutes of Omri are kept; All the works of Ahab’s house are done; And you walk in their counsels, That I may make you a desolation, And your inhabitants a hissing. Therefore you shall bear the reproach of My people.”

WEB.3: My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me!
WEB.4: For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage. I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
WEB.5: My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous acts of Yahweh.”
WEB.6: How shall I come before Yahweh, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
WEB.7: Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams? With tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my disobedience? The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
WEB.8: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
WEB.9: Yahweh’s voice calls to the city, and wisdom sees your name: “Listen to the rod, and he who appointed it.
WEB.10: Are there yet treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and a short ephah  that is accursed?
WEB.11: Shall I be pure with dishonest scales, and with a bag of deceitful weights?

WEB.15: You will sow, but won’t reap. You will tread the olives, but won’t anoint yourself with oil; and crush grapes, but won’t drink the wine.

NLT.1:
Listen to what the LORD is saying: “Stand up and state your case against me.
Let the mountains and hills be called to witness your complaints.
NLT.2:
And now, O mountains,
listen to the LORD’s complaint!
He has a case against his people.
He will bring charges against Israel.
NLT.3:
“O my people, what have I done to you?
What have I done to make you tired of me?
Answer me!
NLT.4:
For I brought you out of Egypt
and redeemed you from slavery.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to help you.
NLT.5:
Don’t you remember, my people,
how King Balak of Moab tried to have you cursed
and how Balaam son of Beor blessed you instead?
And remember your journey from Acacia Grove to Gilgal,
when I, the LORD, did everything I could
to teach you about my faithfulness.”
NLT.6:
What can we bring to the LORD?
Should we bring him burnt offerings?
Should we bow before God Most High
with offerings of yearling calves?
NLT.7:
Should we offer him thousands of rams
and ten thousand rivers of olive oil?
Should we sacrifice our firstborn children
to pay for our sins?
NLT.8:
No, O people, the LORD has told you what is good,
and this is what he requires of you:
to do what is right, to love mercy,
and to walk humbly with your God.
NLT.9:
Fear the LORD if you are wise!
His voice calls to everyone in Jerusalem:
“The armies of destruction are coming;
the LORD is sending them.
NLT.10:
What shall I say about the homes of the wicked
filled with treasures gained by cheating?
What about the disgusting practice
of measuring out grain with dishonest measures?
NLT.11:
How can I tolerate your merchants
who use dishonest scales and weights?
NLT.12:
The rich among you have become wealthy
through extortion and violence.
Your citizens are so used to lying
that their tongues can no longer tell the truth.
NLT.13:
“Therefore, I will wound you!
I will bring you to ruin for all your sins.
NLT.14:
You will eat but never have enough.
Your hunger pangs and emptiness will remain.
And though you try to save your money,
it will come to nothing in the end.
You will save a little,
but I will give it to those who conquer you.
NLT.15:
You will plant crops
but not harvest them.
You will press your olives
but not get enough oil to anoint yourselves.
You will trample the grapes
but get no juice to make your wine.
NLT.16:
You keep only the laws of evil King Omri;
you follow only the example of wicked King Ahab!
Therefore, I will make an example of you,
bringing you to complete ruin.
You will be treated with contempt,
mocked by all who see you.”

AMP.1:
Hear now what the LORD is saying,
"Arise, plead your case before the mountains,
And let the hills [as witnesses] hear your voice.
AMP.2:
"Hear, O mountains, the indictment of the LORD,
And you enduring foundations of the earth,
For the LORD has a case (a legal complaint) against His people,
And He will dispute (challenge) Israel.
AMP.3:
"O My people, what have I done to you [since you have turned away from Me]?
And how have I wearied you? Answer Me.
AMP.4:
"For I brought you up from the land of Egypt
And ransomed you from the house of slavery,
And I sent before you Moses [to lead you], Aaron [the high priest], and Miriam [the prophetess].
AMP.5:
"My people, remember now
What Balak king of Moab devised [with his evil plan against Israel]
And what Balaam the son of Beor answered him [turning the curse into blessing for Israel],
[Remember what the LORD did for you] from Shittim to Gilgal,
So that you may know the righteous and saving acts [displaying the power] of the LORD."
AMP.6:
With what shall I come before the LORD [to honor Him]
And bow myself before God on high?
Shall I come before Him with burnt offerings,
With yearling calves?
AMP.7:
Will the LORD be delighted with thousands of rams,
Or with ten thousand rivers of oil?
Shall I present my firstborn for my acts of rebellion,
The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
AMP.8:
He has told you, O man, what is good;
And what does the LORD require of you
Except to be just, and to love [and to diligently practice] kindness (compassion),
And to walk humbly with your God [setting aside any overblown sense of importance or self-righteousness]?
AMP.9:
The voice of the LORD shall call to the city [of Jerusalem]—
And it is sound wisdom to heed [solemnly] and fear Your name [with awe-filled reverence];
"Hear, O tribe [the rod of punishment]. Who has appointed its time?
AMP.10:
"Are there not still treasures gained by wickedness
In the house of the wicked,
And a short (inaccurate) measure [for grain] that is cursed?
AMP.11:
"Can I [be guiltless and] justify deceptive scales
And a bag of dishonest weights?
AMP.12:
"For the rich men of the city are full of violence [of every kind];
Her inhabitants speak lies
And their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
AMP.13:
"So also I will make you sick, striking you down,
Desolating and devastating you, because of your sins.
AMP.14:
"You shall eat, but you will not be satisfied,
And your emptiness shall be among you;
You will [try to] remove [your goods and those you love] for safekeeping
But you will fail to save anything,
And what you do save I shall give to the sword.
AMP.15:
"You shall sow but you shall not reap;
You shall tread olives, but shall not anoint yourself with oil,
And [you will extract juice from] the grapes, but you shall not drink the wine.
AMP.16:
"For [you have kept] the statutes of Omri [the idolatrous king],
And all the works of the [wicked] house (dynasty) of Ahab;
And you walk in their counsels and policies.
Therefore, I shall hand you over for destruction and horror
And your [city's] inhabitants for ridicule,
And you shall bear the rebuke and scorn of My people."

MSG.1:
Listen now, listen to God:
"Take your stand in court.
If you have a complaint, tell the mountains;
make your case to the hills.
MSG.2:
And now, Mountains, hear God's case;
listen, Jury Earth—
For I am bringing charges against my people.
I am building a case against Israel.
MSG.3:
"Dear people, how have I done you wrong?
Have I burdened you, worn you out? Answer!
MSG.4:
I delivered you from a bad life in Egypt;
I paid a good price to get you out of slavery.
I sent Moses to lead you—
and Aaron and Miriam to boot!
MSG.5:
Remember what Balak king of Moab tried to pull,
and how Balaam son of Beor turned the tables on him.
Remember all those stories about Shittim and Gilgal.
Keep all God's salvation stories fresh and present."
MSG.6:
How can I stand up before God
and show proper respect to the high God?
Should I bring an armload of offerings
topped off with yearling calves?
MSG.7:
Would God be impressed with thousands of rams,
with buckets and barrels of olive oil?
Would he be moved if I sacrificed my firstborn child,
my precious baby, to cancel my sin?
MSG.8:
But he's already made it plain how to live, what to do,
what God is looking for in men and women.
It's quite simple: Do what is fair and just to your neighbor,
be compassionate and loyal in your love,
And don't take yourself too seriously—
take God seriously.
MSG.9:
Attention! God calls out to the city!
If you know what's good for you, you'll listen.
So listen, all of you!
This is serious business.
MSG.10:
"Do you expect me to overlook obscene wealth
you've piled up by cheating and fraud?
MSG.11:
Do you think I'll tolerate shady deals
and shifty scheming?
MSG.12:
I'm tired of the violent rich
bullying their way with bluffs and lies.
MSG.13:
I'm fed up. Beginning now, you're finished.
You'll pay for your sins down to your last cent.
MSG.14:
No matter how much you get, it will never be enough—
hollow stomachs, empty hearts.
No matter how hard you work, you'll have nothing to show for it—
bankrupt lives, wasted souls.
MSG.15:
You'll plant grass
but never get a lawn.
You'll make jelly
but never spread it on your bread.
You'll press apples
but never drink the cider.
MSG.16:
You have lived by the standards of your king, Omri,
the decadent lifestyle of the family of Ahab.
Because you've slavishly followed their fashions,
I'm forcing you into bankruptcy.
Your way of life will be laughed at, a tasteless joke.
Your lives will be derided as futile and fake."

NIV.2:
Hear, O mountains, the Lord’s accusation;
listen, you everlasting foundations of the earth.
For the Lord has a case against his people;
he is lodging a charge against Israel.
NIV.3:
“My people, what have I done to you?
How have I burdened you? Answer me.
NIV.4:
I brought you up out of Egypt
and redeemed you from the land of slavery.
I sent Moses to lead you,
also Aaron and Miriam.
NIV.5:
My people, remember
what Balak king of Moab counseled
and what Balaam son of Beor answered.
Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal,
that you may know the righteous acts of the Lord.”
NIV.6:
With what shall I come before the Lord
and bow down before the exalted God?
Shall I come before him with burnt offerings,
with calves a year old?
NIV.7:
Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams,
with ten thousand rivers of oil?
Shall I offer my firstborn for my transgression,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
NIV.8:
He has showed you, O man, what is good.
And what does the Lord require of you?
To act justly and to love mercy
and to walk humbly with your God.
NIV.9:
Israel’s Guilt and Punishment
Listen! The Lord is calling to the city—
and to fear your name is wisdom—
“Heed the rod and the One who appointed it.
NIV.10:
Am I still to forget, O wicked house,
your ill-gotten treasures
and the short ephah, which is accursed?
NIV.11:
Shall I acquit a man with dishonest scales,
with a bag of false weights?
NIV.12:
Her rich men are violent;
her people are liars
and their tongues speak deceitfully.
NIV.13:
Therefore, I have begun to destroy you,
to ruin you because of your sins.
NIV.14:
You will eat but not be satisfied;
your stomach will still be empty.
You will store up but save nothing,
because what you save I will give to the sword.
NIV.15:
You will plant but not harvest;
you will press olives but not use the oil on yourselves,
you will crush grapes but not drink the wine.
NIV.16:
You have observed the statutes of Omri
and all the practices of Ahab’s house,
and you have followed their traditions.
Therefore I will give you over to ruin
and your people to derision;
you will bear the scorn of the nations.”

NET.1: Listen to what the LORD says: “Get up! Defend yourself before the mountains! Present your case before the hills!”
NET.2: Hear the LORD’s accusation, you mountains, you enduring foundations of the earth! For the LORD has a case against his people; he has a dispute with Israel!
NET.3: “My people, how have I wronged you? How have I wearied you? Answer me!
NET.4: In fact, I brought you up from the land of Egypt, I delivered you from that place of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead you.
NET.5: My people, recall how King Balak of Moab planned to harm you, how Balaam son of Beor responded to him. Recall how you journeyed from Shittim to Gilgal, so you might acknowledge that the LORD has treated you fairly.”
NET.6: With what should I enter the LORD’s presence? With what should I bow before the sovereign God? Should I enter his presence with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
NET.7: Will the LORD accept a thousand rams, or ten thousand streams of olive oil? Should I give him my firstborn child as payment for my rebellion, my offspring — my own flesh and blood — for my sin?
NET.8: He has told you, O man, what is good, and what the LORD really wants from you: He wants you to promote justice, to be faithful, and to live obediently before your God.
NET.9: Listen! The LORD is calling to the city! It is wise to respect your authority, O LORD! Listen, O nation, and those assembled in the city!
NET.10: “I will not overlook, O sinful house, the dishonest gain you have hoarded away, or the smaller-than-standard measure I hate so much.
NET.11: I do not condone the use of rigged scales, or a bag of deceptive weights.
NET.12: The city’s rich men think nothing of resorting to violence; her inhabitants lie, their tongues speak deceptive words.
NET.13: I will strike you brutally and destroy you because of your sin.
NET.14: You will eat, but not be satisfied. Even if you have the strength to overtake some prey, you will not be able to carry it away; if you do happen to carry away something, I will deliver it over to the sword.
NET.15: You will plant crops, but will not harvest them; you will squeeze oil from the olives, but you will have no oil to rub on your bodies; you will squeeze juice from the grapes, but you will have no wine to drink.
NET.16: You implement the regulations of Omri, and all the practices of Ahab’s dynasty; you follow their policies. Therefore I will make you an appalling sight, the city’s inhabitants will be taunted derisively, and nations will mock all of you.”

NRSVCE.1:
Hear what the LORD says:
Rise, plead your case before the mountains,
and let the hills hear your voice.
NRSVCE.2:
Hear, you mountains, the controversy of the LORD,
and you enduring foundations of the earth;
for the LORD has a controversy with his people,
and he will contend with Israel.
NRSVCE.3:
“O my people, what have I done to you?
In what have I wearied you? Answer me!
NRSVCE.4:
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt,
and redeemed you from the house of slavery;
and I sent before you Moses,
Aaron, and Miriam.
NRSVCE.5:
O my people, remember now what King Balak of Moab devised,
what Balaam son of Beor answered him,
and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal,
that you may know the saving acts of the LORD.”
NRSVCE.6:
“With what shall I come before the LORD,
and bow myself before God on high?
Shall I come before him with burnt offerings,
with calves a year old?
NRSVCE.7:
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams,
with ten thousands of rivers of oil?
Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression,
the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?”
NRSVCE.8:
He has told you, O mortal, what is good;
and what does the LORD require of you
but to do justice, and to love kindness,
and to walk humbly with your God?
NRSVCE.9:
The voice of the LORD cries to the city
(it is sound wisdom to fear your name):
Hear, O tribe and assembly of the city!
NRSVCE.10:
Can I forget the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked,
and the scant measure that is accursed?
NRSVCE.11:
Can I tolerate wicked scales
and a bag of dishonest weights?
NRSVCE.12:
Your wealthy are full of violence;
your inhabitants speak lies,
with tongues of deceit in their mouths.
NRSVCE.13:
Therefore I have begun to strike you down,
making you desolate because of your sins.
NRSVCE.14:
You shall eat, but not be satisfied,
and there shall be a gnawing hunger within you;
you shall put away, but not save,
and what you save, I will hand over to the sword.
NRSVCE.15:
You shall sow, but not reap;
you shall tread olives, but not anoint yourselves with oil;
you shall tread grapes, but not drink wine.
NRSVCE.16:
For you have kept the statutes of Omri
and all the works of the house of Ahab,
and you have followed their counsels.
Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of hissing;
so you shall bear the scorn of my people.
